thread:
kai: quick issue — customers on older SDKs are getting surprise flips when we deprecate v1. thinking about a console "soft-pin" affordance to temporarily pin tokens to their current version during a deprec rollout.

tasha: soft-pin = per-token TTL pin to served version? sounds like it could reduce user-visible churn. what's the default TTL?

kai: proposal: 5m for typical fallbacks, but console-exposed option for tenants doing migrations to set 1h or 24h. pin created when a fallback happens or when tenant opts in.

ben: billing/quotas: if we pin to v1, we should attribute usage to the served variant. finance wants an audit tag `pin_reason=deprec` and `pin_ttl`.

mira: implementation note: routing writes a signed affinity entry keyed by token_id -> {version, origin=soft-pin, ttl}. routing checks affinity before route selection. no client headers accepted.

tasha: console UX: show per-route toggle "Enable soft-pin on fallback" and a small explainer. default OFF; internal tenants can enable for canaries.

ben: telemetry: emit `pin.created`, `pin.expired`, `pin.applied` with tenant and route. also surface a metric for "pinned_units" so ops can see load shift.

kai: safety: add a per-variant capacity cap so we don't accidentally shift too much load to legacy pools. if cap exceeded, stop creating new pins and emit `pin.rejected_capacity`.

mira: edgecases: streaming sessions should keep original affinity; soft-pin only applies to new requests not in active streams.

ops-bot: feature flagged deploy scheduled: routing/soft-pin canary -> internal at 2024-12-08T09:00:00Z.

tasha: I'll draft brief console copy and rollout checklist. ben will sync with finance on export fields. kai will open RFC and PRs.
